component.name: Idasen Companion
component.summary: Automatic sit/stand companion for the IKEA Idåsen desk

description.p: Idasen Companion alternates your IKEA Idåsen desk between sitting and standing based on active time at the computer — time spent idle or with the session locked doesn't count. A background daemon owns the Bluetooth connection and the automation logic; a Qt 6 tray application gives you live status, manual controls, presets, scheduling, statistics and desktop notifications.

ul.li: Active-time automation with lenient and strict idle thresholds, so the desk never moves while you might be away.
Cycle variation so sit/stand transitions don't feel mechanical.
Interruption handling — the resulting height is verified after every move and retried if you grabbed the paddle mid-move.
On-demand Bluetooth that connects only when there's work, then drops the connection.
Manual sit/stand and preset controls, scheduling, per-day statistics and an activity log.

description.p: This is an independent, unofficial project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Inter IKEA Systems B.V. IKEA and Idåsen are trademarks of their respective owners.

description.p: Refreshed application and tray icons include artwork for small desktop sizes and HiDPI displays. Debian packages now include the SVG icon-loading plugin.
Package checks better detect missing translations, and release titles consistently show the version number.
The installed command now opens the desktop app or runs desk controls from the terminal. Headless packages keep the command-line controls and background service without Qt.
Bluetooth operations are bounded, Stop prevents stale moves, and session switching releases only this app's desk connection.
Adds a localized, Qt-free command-line client for status, recent activity and desk control, plus smaller headless RPM and Debian packages containing only the client and daemon.

Number, date, time and unit formatting is now consistent across the desktop, daemon and command line. A new clock-format setting controls every displayed time, newer configuration options survive edits by older versions, and translated or right-to-left layouts adapt more reliably.
Fixes two places on the Statistics page that showed English text whatever language the rest of the window was in: the labels under the range slider, and the tooltip on the daily chart.
Text throughout the window is now translated as whole sentences rather than assembled from pieces, so a translation can order the words the way its own language does.
The package now carries everything it needs to run, so it installs on any RPM-based distribution rather than on one release of Fedora.
The window follows the desktop's theme more closely, including a switch between light and dark while it is open. The activity log groups its entries by day and redraws without stuttering.
Fixes a Bluetooth connection to the desk that stayed open across a suspend and never closed on waking, keeping other apps from reaching the desk until it was disconnected by hand.
Fixes the screenshots on this page, which named files that were not part of the 1.0.0 release.
First public release. The desk alternates between sitting and standing on active time at the computer, and stands down while you are idle, locked or away.

Includes manual sit/stand and preset controls, scheduling, per-day statistics and an activity log, a tray application with desktop notifications, on-demand Bluetooth, and English and Spanish translations.
First packaged release, shipping as an RPM, a .deb and a Flatpak bundle.
